title: Browser Cookie Theft
overview: Investigate a sensitive browser session-store access by a non-browser process.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and windows security or sysmon projection fields.

attack.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A non-browser process reading the session store without approval warrants checking file and identity telemetry.
evidence: Identify caller, target classification and operation. Compare application session changes for the same user.
false_positive: Authorized profile backup, migration or endpoint response tools can read the store.
tuning: Allow only reviewed, signed tooling with explicit purpose and bounded access.
response: Preserve endpoint evidence, validate access scope and revoke sessions if there is evidence of unintended access.
prevention: Restrict process access, enforce session protections and monitor browser profile access.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The episode contains access metadata only, with no browser files or session cookies.

options: The identity and authorization of the reader
questions.explanation: The same store can be accessed legitimately by the browser.

questions.prompt: What reduces the risk of continued session misuse?
questions.explanation: Revocation terminates existing authorization where supported.
